name: yet

phase_0.boundary_condition: the narrative frame that contains both events and their paradoxical relation

VINIT.justification: void state before any event or expectation exists

TANCH.justification: boundary closing the scenario where 'yet' applies

AFWD.justification: forward morphism from event X to the expected blocking of Y

AREV.justification: reverse morphism from actual Y occurrence back to the cancelled expectation

CLINK.justification: composition of event X then event Y in time

IMSCRIB.justification: self-identity referring to itself as a linguistic and logical operator

FSPLIT.justification: splits into two possible worlds: prevention succeeds (Y absent) and fails (Y present)

FFUSE.justification: merges the two branches back into the single concept that contains both expectation and violation

EVALT.justification: affirmative branch: Y actually happens despite expectation

EVALF.justification: negative branch: Y does not happen (expected outcome)

ENGAGR.justification: holds both the expectation and its violation simultaneously, paradice state

IFIX.justification: permanent fixation of the statement in discourse

split_outputs: world where prevention succeeds (Y does not occur)

phase_3.void_description: no events, no expectations, no temporal order — pure potentiality
phase_3.true_description: occurrence of Y — affirmation of the actual outcome
phase_3.false_description: non-occurrence of Y — affirmation of the expected prevention
phase_3.both_description: simultaneous holding of both expectation and its violation — the paradoxical core of 'yet'

steps.domain_action: narrative boundary closed around the eventual scenario
the concept 'yet' enters as self-referent operator
event X occurs, forward morphism toward prevention inference
X composed with expected prevention (if prevention holds, Y blocked)
split into two possible worlds — where prevention succeeds (F-arm) and fails (T-arm)
on F-arm, Y does not occur (expected outcome, false state)
on T-arm, Y occurs despite expectation (actual outcome, true state)
both arms held simultaneously as the paradox of 'yet'
arms merged back into the single concept 'yet' that contains both possibilities
forward propagation of the resolved paradox
utterance of 'X yet Y' recorded permanently

phase_5.compiler_frontend: the generative grammar that produces 'yet' statements from event sequences
phase_5.memory_mechanism: temporal trace storing event order and expectations
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: the logical ordering of events and their causal relations
phase_5.alfs_store: natural language lexicon entry for 'yet' as a conjunction

phase_6.cycle_cost: one unit of logical tension per 'yet' usage
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — the cycle merely reorganizes logical tension without dissipating it
